current.text: Verify that if a credential has to be used for service authentication, the credential being used by the consumer is not a default credential (e.g., root/root or admin/admin).

master.text: Verify that if a credential has to be used for service authentication, the credential being used by the consumer is not a default credential (e.g., root/root or admin/admin).

predecessors.text: Verify that if passwords are required for service authentication, the service account used is not a default credential. (e.g. root/root or admin/admin are default in some services during installation).

summaries.body:
The 5.0 mapping records V13.2.3 as a grammar move from 4.0.3 V2.10.2: if passwords are required for service authentication, the service account must not be a default credential such as root/root or admin/admin. The current clause keeps that meaning, substituting "if a credential has to be used" and "the credential being used by the consumer." Mapping is the reliable origin.

Issue 475, despite the V13.2.3 title, is Elar Lang's 21 February 2019 request to drop Referer checks from REST CSRF protection in the old API chapter. vanderaj resolved that occupant of the ID on 26 February 2019. Those API/malicious-code git events do not attest this default-credential control.

The mapping classifies the 4.0.3-to-5.0 change as grammar: "passwords"/"service account" became "credential"/"consumer," and the installation-default parenthetical was shortened. No other attested wording change bears on this clause.

Git at the V13.2.3 slot is the old REST CSRF item: jim's 22 February 2019 API-file update, vanderaj resolving issues 475 and 566 on 26 February 2019, and elar's 25 April 2020 header-naming corrections. Skip those as ID-slot reuse.
